turns.prompt_text: can you create a an action when I say a specific label or name
turns.response_html:
To create an action based on a specific label or name, you need to use a programming language or an automation tool that supports conditional logic.

If...then statements are the most common way to achieve this. The structure would look like this:

if [label/name] is [specific label/name] then [perform action]

For example, using Python:

label = "urgent"

if label == "urgent":
    print("Sending a high-priority notification.")

In this example, the code checks if the label variable is equal to the string "urgent". If it is, it executes the action of printing "Sending a high-priority notification.".

Many automation platforms like IFTTT (If This Then That) or Zapier provide a user-friendly interface to set up these kinds of rules without writing code. You would simply choose a trigger (the specific label or name) and an action to perform.

turns.prompt_text: when I say open D50 printer can you open print Master every time
turns.response_html: You can create custom voice commands on your computer to open a specific application. Windows has a built-in "Voice Access" feature where you can create shortcuts. On a Mac, you can use "Voice Control" to create new commands that launch an app or perform an action.

turns.prompt_text: do you have a custom voice commands
turns.response_html: While I don't have personal custom voice commands, you can set up shortcuts on your device to create commands that trigger specific actions. Many voice assistants and operating systems offer this feature.

turns.prompt_text: can you show me where in settings I can see this feature
turns.response_html:
The location of custom voice commands varies by operating system.

For Windows:

  1. Go to Settings.
  2. Click on Accessibility.
  3. Select Speech.
  4. Toggle on Voice Access.
  5. Once Voice Access is enabled, you can say "show commands" and then "Voice shortcuts" to create a new command.

For Mac:

  1. Go to the Apple menu.
  2. Open System Settings.
  3. Click on Accessibility in the sidebar.
  4. Select Voice Control.
  5. Click on Commands... to view and create new commands.
